local_facts.title: Bicyclists and pedestrians account for most fatal and severe injuries in the city
local_facts.claim: Santa Barbara’s 2026 Safe Streets for All safety analysis reports that bicyclists were involved in 42% and pedestrians in 17% of the City’s fatal and severe injury collisions; it also reports that 62% of injury collisions occur at intersections.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A collision involving a person walking or biking, especially at an intersection or along the dense coastal grid, needs early attention to the exact crossing, travel path, sight lines, witnesses, and any available video. Citywide figures do not decide fault in an individual claim.

local_facts.title: Santa Barbara County civil matters have a local court home
local_facts.claim: Santa Barbara County Superior Court identifies its Anacapa Division at 1100 Anacapa Street in Santa Barbara as handling Civil matters, along with several other case types.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A crash claim that requires civil litigation follows Santa Barbara County’s local court structure. Long before filing is considered, a well-organized file of collision, medical, financial, witness, and insurance records is useful.

local_facts.title: Isla Vista and UCSB bring a major daily bike-and-pedestrian travel pattern
local_facts.claim: The Isla Vista Community Services District says more than 10,000 people commute daily from their homes to campus and notes more than seven miles of bike paths in the UCSB campus area.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A collision involving a UCSB or Isla Vista trip may require early investigation of a bicycle or scooter route, a campus-area witness, a borrowed vehicle, and applicable insurance documents instead of treating it as a generic roadway claim.

anchors.label: An unconscionable or illegal fee
anchors.detail: That is the whole of California's substantive limit on an injury fee. Unconscionability is judged on the facts existing when the agreement was made, using thirteen enumerated factors.
anchors.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(a)

anchors.label: Any paper requiring a hearing, Santa Barbara Superior Court
anchors.detail: Payable on discovery motions, motions to continue a trial date, motions for new trial and ex parte applications requiring notice, unless it is the party's first paper.
anchors.source_name: Santa Barbara Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 45

anchors.label: Summary judgment or summary adjudication motion
anchors.detail: The single most expensive routine filing in a civil case, and the one an insurer is most likely to bring in a disputed-liability crash claim.
anchors.source_name: Santa Barbara Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 51

anchors.label: Malpractice fee ceiling, and only malpractice
anchors.detail: The statutory limit on a contingency fee in a professional negligence action against a health care provider. It has no application to a motor vehicle claim.

fee_rows.stage: Testing a fee after the fact
fee_rows.note: Overreaching, undisclosed material facts, proportion to the value of services, sophistication of the parties, difficulty, result, time spent, informed consent, and more.
fee_rows.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(b)

fee_rows.stage: Language the contract has to contain
fee_rows.note: Outside malpractice claims, the contract must say in terms that the fee is not set by law but negotiable, and the plaintiff leaves with a signed duplicate.
Santa Barbara charges the uniform statewide amount; no local courthouse construction surcharge applies in this county.
fee_rows.source_name: Santa Barbara Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 1

fee_rows.note: One hundred fifty dollars nonrefundable to preserve a jury, and thirty dollars for reporting a civil proceeding lasting an hour or less.
fee_rows.source_name: Santa Barbara Superior Court civil fee schedule, items 64 and 66

fee_rows.stage: Moving the case to another county
fee_rows.note: Processing a change of venue, paid to the court the transfer is requested from. It arrives when a defendant is based elsewhere.
fee_rows.source_name: Santa Barbara Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 55

fee_rows.stage: Splitting a fee with an outside firm
fee_rows.note: The division needs a written agreement between the firms, the client's written consent after full disclosure of the terms, and no increase in the total fee.
fee_rows.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5.1(a)
